recreation_brief:
1. Create a blank white PowerPoint slide.
2. Draw thick blue grid lines dividing the slide into roughly a 3x3 grid (vertical line at ~35% from left, horizontal lines at ~35% and ~75% from top).
3. In the top-left cell, draw a red-bordered rectangle. Inside it, place a smaller red-bordered box at top with text 'Threshold=0.0'. Below that, create a 2x2 table with header 'Predicted as', column headers P and N, row headers P and N (with 'Actual' rotated vertically on the far left), and cell values: row P: 5, 0; row N: 6, 0.
4. To the right of that table inside the same panel, add a light yellow box with two lines: 'TPR=5/(5+0)=1' and 'FPR=6/(6+0)=1'.
5. In the top-right corner of the slide, draw a yellow circle with the number '29' inside.
6. In the large right-middle panel (approx 65-100% width, 0-75% height), draw a blue-bordered rectangle with light cyan fill. Add vertical y-axis label 'TPR' and horizontal x-axis label 'FPR'. Draw light gray grid lines. Place a single red-outlined circle at the top-right corner of the plot area with a label box '0.0' next to it. Optionally add a mouse cursor icon in the plot area.
7. In the bottom-right area, stack two white formula boxes: 'TPR = TP / TP + FN' and 'FPR = FP / FP + TN'. To their right, create a 2x2 confusion matrix with header 'Predicted as', columns P and N, rows P and N. Color the cells: TP light red, FN yellow, FP yellow, TN light green.
8. In the bottom-center cell, draw a gray rounded rectangle with text 'ROC Curve for Same Model -different thresholds'.
9. Use black sans-serif text for all labels and values throughout.
